title: What a polish pass finds
lede: Nothing structural, which is the interesting part. The shape of the guide was sound and the drift was in the sentences.
body: We walked every record against the contract, expecting to find broken entries and finding none. What the pass turned up instead was drift: three records written in a register the other 192 do not use, eight links that rendered nowhere, and three sightings that never named the thing they were sighting.

The voice problem is the one worth writing down. [Crookmaxxing](/moves/crookmaxxing/), [JAQing Off](/moves/jaqing-off/) and [Bootcurious](/buffs/bootcurious/) carried part-of-speech markers inside their senses, in italics, and a long explanatory clause where the book uses an epigram. The part of speech already has a field. The senses now open the way the rest of their kind opens, and Bootcurious stopped describing a person when it is filed as a condition that expires.

The dead links are the failure this guide is most likely to have. Eight records listed a term under both the related list and the confused-with pair. Both generators drop the twin from the related list, because the pair edge already renders it, so the link was authored, validated, and shown to nobody. A rule enforced in two places is a rule that eventually gets satisfied in neither.

The graph had drifted too. [The transcript](/remedies/the-transcript/) was named in the counter prose of Heckler's veto and Rally and was not wired to either, so the page told you to publish the transcript and did not offer you the entry that says how. Both edges are in now, and Rally no longer claims a habitat commits a fallacy it merely houses.

A polish pass is not a feature. It is the maintenance that keeps a field guide usable after a hundred small additions, and the finding is always the same: the entries are fine, the joins are where it rots.
